sceneFacts.shortVersion: This film launched director Tim Story's career.
sceneFacts.longDescription: This film launched director Tim Story's career. Made on a $12 million budget, it grossed $77 million at the box office.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 0] 00:00:00–00:00:12
summary: The video clip displays the Metro Goldwyn Mayer (MGM) logo featuring a lion, typically used as an opening sequence for movies.
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: Barbershop's commercial success, grossing $77 million worldwide on a $12 million budget, was pivotal in launching director Tim Story's career, leading him to direct films like 2005's Fantastic Four.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Music in the film turns street fights into dance breaks.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Music in the film turns street fights into dance breaks. This diegetic choice makes music feel like a shop fixture, not a narrator.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 7] 00:02:18–00:02:35
summary: The clip shows a tense and angry confrontation between individuals in a dark, possibly indoor environment, with aggressive dialogue and a flashlight being shone in someone's face.
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: The film strategically used diegetic music, like Marvin Gaye's "Got to Give It Up (Part 1)" to diffuse a street confrontation into a dance break, and EPMD's "You Gots to Chill" to unite barbershop patrons.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Ice Cube really got into character as Calvin, even suggesting glasses.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Ice Cube really got into character as Calvin, even suggesting glasses. He identified with Calvin as a man trying to do the right thing and run a respectable business.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 14] 00:04:39–00:04:59
summary: A man speaks with frustration and disappointment about being late for work and the challenges he faces, conveying a somber and tense mood in a dimly lit indoor setting.
cast on screen: Ice Cube

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Calvin was originally written for an older actor.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Calvin was originally written for an older actor. Director Tim Story and the producers decided to make the character younger.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 22] 00:07:16–00:07:36
summary: Two men engage in a casual, humorous conversation about a haircut style and money in a warmly lit indoor setting, possibly a barbershop, with a third man joining the discussion.
cast on screen: Ice Cube
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: The character of Calvin, played by Ice Cube, was initially written for an older actor, but the creators decided to make him younger, leading to Ice Cube's casting.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: The cast went to barber school to learn how to cut hair.
sceneFacts.longDescription: The cast went to barber school to learn how to cut hair. Director Tim Story had the entire cast attend a barbering class for several days before filming.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 59] 00:19:38–00:19:58
summary: The clip shows a group of people inside a barbershop where one person is getting a haircut while others engage in a humorous and slightly irritated conversation about missing apple juice, creating a casual and comedic atmosphere.
cast on screen: Michael Ealy, Eve, Ice Cube

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Eddie's an old-time barber with strong opinions and no customers.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Eddie's an old-time barber with strong opinions and no customers. He's also known for having a big mouth.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 111] 00:36:59–00:37:14
summary: The clip shows men interacting in a barbershop, with one man getting a shave while others talk and joke, creating a casual and friendly mood in an indoor social setting.
cast on screen: Ice Cube, Cedric The Entertainer, Troy Garity
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: Cedric the Entertainer was 37 years old when he played the elder barber Eddie, a role originally conceived for an older, veteran character actor.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Eddie's controversial jokes were meant to spark real conversations.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Eddie's controversial jokes were meant to spark real conversations. Filmmakers wanted to show diverse opinions, not a monolithic Black viewpoint.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 170] 00:56:16–00:56:35
summary: The video clip shows a group of men in a social setting engaging in a heated and provocative discussion about controversial historical and cultural figures, creating a tense and confrontational mood.
cast on screen: Deray Davis, Cedric The Entertainer, Michael Ealy, Troy Garity, Eve
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: Filmmakers, including writer Don Scott, defended Eddie's controversial jokes as an intentional effort to portray diverse, uncensored conversations in a real barbershop and challenge the notion of a monolithic Black viewpoint.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Cedric the Entertainer chose to play Eddie, and it changed his career.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Cedric the Entertainer chose to play Eddie, and it changed his career. He was initially cast as the ATM thief J.D. but insisted on playing the old-timer.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 222] 01:13:01–01:13:39
summary: The clip shows a man in a dimly lit room expressing frustration and anger while discussing racial economic disparities and social issues, with other characters contributing to a tense conversation about wealth and race in America.
cast on screen: Cedric The Entertainer, Ice Cube

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Director Tim Story encouraged the cast to bring their own ideas to scenes.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Director Tim Story encouraged the cast to bring their own ideas to scenes. He believed actors of this caliber should contribute their own ideas.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 222] 01:13:01–01:13:39
summary: The clip shows a man in a dimly lit room expressing frustration and anger while discussing racial economic disparities and social issues, with other characters contributing to a tense conversation about wealth and race in America.
cast on screen: Cedric The Entertainer, Ice Cube
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: Director Tim Story encouraged significant improvisation from the cast, which contributed to the film's raw and authentic feel, including many unscripted moments.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Cedric the Entertainer's improv changed how scenes were shot.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Cedric the Entertainer's improv changed how scenes were shot. Director Tim Story couldn't storyboard his spontaneous movements.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 222] 01:13:01–01:13:39
summary: The clip shows a man in a dimly lit room expressing frustration and anger while discussing racial economic disparities and social issues, with other characters contributing to a tense conversation about wealth and race in America.
cast on screen: Cedric The Entertainer, Ice Cube
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: Director Tim Story initially used extensive storyboarding, but the cast's improvisational talents, especially Cedric the Entertainer's, meant storyboards couldn't fully capture every spontaneous moment.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Barbershop's success led to a whole cinematic universe.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Barbershop's success led to a whole cinematic universe. It spawned a sequel, a spin-off film, and a TV series.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: The film's story was originally set in Los Angeles.
sceneFacts.longDescription: The film's story was originally set in Los Angeles. Producers Robert Teitel and George Tillman Jr. moved the setting to their hometown of Chicago.
